unit.title: Flourishing and detachment
unit.needIt: This helps you stay calm when things go wrong by teaching you to focus only on what you can control. It helps you stop stressing over traffic, the weather, or what other people think of you.
unit.why: A man named Epictetus lived as a slave but found freedom by changing how he thought about his life. He taught that we only suffer when we try to control things that are not up to us. By letting go of the outside world, he found a way to stay steady even when life was hard.
unit.outcome: Distinguish between things you can change and things you cannot.
unit.reachesYou: You feel this when you get stuck in a long line at a store and feel your blood pressure rise. You also feel it when you worry about a mean comment on your phone that you cannot take back.
unit.do: Identify one thing today that is bothering you and ask yourself if it is actually under your control.

quiz.q: What was the primary goal of the Stoic worldview?
quiz.why: Stoics believed the world has an order and humans should act in accord with reason.
quiz.quote: And that the responsibility of human beings, given that order, is to cultivate a particular kind of virtue.

quiz.q: What does Epictetus suggest we do with our perceptions?
quiz.why: He wants us to see things in a way that does not harm us.
quiz.quote: You need to alter your perceptions of the world so that you come to apprehend things in such a way that they don't influence you harmfully.

quiz.q: What is the 'mistake' Epictetus warns against?
choices: Confusing what is ours with what is not
quiz.why: Thinking you can control things you cannot leads to misery.
quiz.quote: The mistake of confusing that over which you have control and that over which you lack control leads to thwarted, upset, miserable, blamingness.

quiz.q: How does Epictetus suggest we handle our desires?
choices: Make our desires fit the world
quiz.why: He argues that we should want things to happen as they do happen.
quiz.quote: Do not want to have events happen to you as you want them to, but instead want them to happen as they do happen.

quiz.q: What does Stockdale say is the most harmful thing?
quiz.why: He argues that destroying your internal character is the true harm.
quiz.quote: Epictetus, look not for any greater harm than this, destroying the trustworthy, self-respecting, well-behaved man inside you.

decoys.text: You should ignore your social relations.

crystal.aha: By separating what you can control from what you cannot, you find peace.
